**Proposed mechanism:** FOXL2 (HGNC:3767) —LEADS_TO→ Ptosis (HP:0000508); FOXL2 (HGNC:3767) —LEADS_TO→ Epicanthus inversus (HP:0000204); FOXL2 (HGNC:3767) —LEADS_TO→ Blepharophimosis, ptosis, and epicanthus inversus (HP:0000492); SUMO1 (HGNC:11056) —DISRUPTS→ SUMOylation pathway (GO:0000170); SUMOylation pathway (GO:0000170) —LEADS_TO→ Orofacial cleft (HP:0000218). Loss-of-function mutations in SUMO1 disrupt the SUMOylation pathway, leading to orofacial clefting. Haploinsufficiency of FOXL2, a transcription factor, results in BPES, which includes ptosis and epicanthus inversus. The SUMOylation pathway, regulated by SUMO1, is crucial for various cellular processes including craniofacial development, thus providing a mechanistic link to orofacial clefting.

**How to falsify it:** The absence of SUMO1 mutations in patients with orofacial cleft 10, or the presence of SUMO1 mutations in individuals without orofacial cleft 10, would falsify this hypothesis. Furthermore, if genetic studies reveal no involvement of the SUMOylation pathway in craniofacial development, this hypothesis would be refuted. _(variant: A common pathogenic variant in SUMO1 (e.g., allele frequency > 1% in gnomAD) associated with OFC10 would challenge its role as a rare disease gene.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of the SUMOylation pathway in craniofacial development could lead to novel therapeutic targets for orofacial clefting disorders and potentially inform management strategies for BPES.
